S.FORM: sua iiku ia, muʔu. tee=ku pu-a-iisua ma-maaraŋ miana, kanakanavu mata pakisia.
S.PHON: sua iiku ia muʔu teeku puaiisua mamaaraŋ miana kanakanavu mata pakiʂia
S.FORM: sua iiku ia, mu'u. teeku puaiisua mamaarang miana, kanakanavu mata pakisia.
S.PHON: sua iiku ia muʔu teeku puaiisua mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana kanakanavu mata pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: I am Mu'u. I will talk about the story that happened between the Kanakanavu and Chinese elders in the past.

S.FORM: sua tia=kari=maku ia, ʔuuna=kani ma-maaraŋ kanakanavu miana, ʔuuna=kan ma-maaraŋ pakisia.
S.PHON: sua tiakarimaku ia ʔuunakani mamaaraŋ kanakanavu miana ʔuunakan mamaaraŋ pakiʂia
S.FORM: sua tiakarimaku ia, 'uunakani mamaarang kanakanavu miana, 'uunakan mamaarang pakisia.
S.PHON: sua tiaka[r|ɾ]imaku ia ʔuunakani mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ kanakanavu miana ʔuunakan mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: My story involves Kanakanavu and Chinese elders in the past.

S.FORM: pu-a-iisua sua tia=tu-ʔuna-a-in, pu-a-iisua sua si-a-kaən-in.
S.PHON: puaiisua sua tiatuʔunaain puaiisua sua ʂiakaənin
S.FORM: puaiisua sua tiatu'unaain, puaiisua sua siakaenin.
S.PHON: puaiisua sua tiatuʔunaain puaiisua sua ʂiakaenin
S.TRANSL: (They) discussed their places of residence and the utensils they used for eating.

S.FORM: masi-ʔulu=kani sua pakisia, makasi-in=kani=kiai ma-maaraŋ kanakanavu.
S.PHON: maʂiʔuɾukani sua pakiʂia makaʂiinkanikiai mamaaraŋ kanakanavu
S.FORM: masi'urukani sua pakisia, makasiinkanikiai mamaarang kanakanavu.
S.PHON: maʂiʔu[r|ɾ]ukani sua pakiʂia makaʂiinkanikiai mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: The Chinese people spoke first, and they said this to the Kanakanavu elders.

S.FORM: "sua naanu? sua taka-ʔanman-an=mu tee=kara=kamu? mu-a-ʔuna tantanau sa tee=kara=kamu, mu-a-ʔuna ta-niŋiniŋ-a?" misa=kani sua pakisia.
S.PHON: sua naanu sua takaʔanmananmu teekarakamu muaʔuna tantanau sa teekarakamu muaʔuna taniŋiniŋa misakani sua pakiʂia
S.FORM: "sua naanu? sua taka'anmananmu teekarakamu? mua'una tantanau sa teekarakamu, mua'una taningininga?" misakani sua pakisia.
S.PHON: sua naanu sua takaʔanmananmu teeka[r|ɾ]akamu muaʔuna tantanau sa teeka[r|ɾ]akamu muaʔuna taniŋiniŋa misakani sua pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: "Where do you like to live? Do you prefer living in the mountains or on the plains?" the Chinese people asked.

S.FORM: m-ali-vali=kani ma-maaraŋ kanakanavu, "tokkiaʔai," misai=kani.
S.PHON: maɾivaɾikani mamaaraŋ kanakanavu tokkiaʔai misaikani
S.FORM: marivarikani mamaarang kanakanavu, "tokkia'ai," misaikani.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]ikani mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ kanakanavu tokkiaʔai misaikani
S.TRANSL: The Kanakanavu elders answered, "(We) don't know."

S.FORM: pasi-vali-ai=kani ma-maaraŋ kanakanavu sua pakisia.
S.PHON: paʂivaɾiaikani mamaaraŋ kanakanavu sua pakiʂia
S.FORM: pasivariaikani mamaarang kanakanavu sua pakisia.
S.PHON: paʂiva[r|ɾ]iaikani mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ kanakanavu sua pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: The Kanakanavu elders answered the Chinese people.

S.FORM: makasua-ini ia, "tee=kamu mu-a-ʔuna naanu?" kisa-ən=kani=kiai pakisia.
S.PHON: makasuaini ia teekamu muaʔuna naanu kisaənkanikiai pakiʂia
S.FORM: makasuaini ia, "teekamu mua'una naanu?" kisaenkanikiai pakisia.
S.PHON: makasuaini ia teekamu muaʔuna naanu kisaenkanikiai pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: Then they asked the Chinese people, "Where will you live?"

S.FORM: m-ali-nalusu=kani ma-maaraŋ pakisia m-ali-vali.
S.PHON: maɾinaɾusukani mamaaraŋ pakiʂia maɾivaɾi
S.FORM: marinarusukani mamaarang pakisia marivari.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]ina[r|ɾ]usukani mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ pakiʂia ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i
S.TRANSL: The Chinese people immediately answered.

S.FORM: "tee=kimi mu-a-ʔuna ta-niŋiniŋ-a," misai=kani sua pakisia.
S.PHON: teekimi muaʔuna taniŋiniŋa misaikani sua pakiʂia
S.FORM: "teekimi mua'una taningininga," misaikani sua pakisia.
S.PHON: teekimi muaʔuna taniŋiniŋa misaikani sua pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: "We will live on the plains," the Chinese people said.

S.FORM: nain vanai-n? nai, cəʔəra-i, pu-a-iisua ia, kaʔan pu-a-rəsəvə sua pakisia.
S.PHON: nain vanain nai ʦəʔərai puaiisua ia kaʔan puarəsəvə sua pakiʂia
S.FORM: nain vanain? nai, ce'erai, puaiisua ia, ka'an puareseve sua pakisia.
S.PHON: nain vanain nai ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]ai puaiisua ia kaʔan pua[r|ɾ]eseve sua pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: How could this be? Look, (they) discussed it, the Chinese people did not lie.

S.FORM: nai, cəʔəra-i, pakisia mu-a-ʔuna maamia ta-niŋiniŋ-a, mu-a-ʔuna=kita maamia tantanau rəmər-a calulu. nain sua taavalaʔ-an=ta?
S.PHON: nai ʦəʔərai pakiʂia muaʔuna maamia taniŋiniŋa muaʔunakita maamia tantanau rəməra ʦaɾuɾu nain sua taavaɾaʔanta
S.FORM: nai, ce'erai, pakisia mua'una maamia taningininga, mua'unakita maamia tantanau remera caruru. nain sua taavara'anta?
S.PHON: nai ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]ai pakiʂia muaʔuna maamia taniŋiniŋa muaʔunakita maamia tantanau [r|ɾ]eme[r|ɾ]a ʦa[r|ɾ]u[r|ɾ]u nain sua taava[r|ɾ]aʔanta
S.TRANSL: Look, the Chinese people live on the plains, while we live in the high mountains. What do we know?

S.FORM: makasua=cu ŋuai-ni, tee=kani=cu pu-a-iisua sua tia=si-a-kaən-ini.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu ŋuaini teekaniʦu puaiisua sua tiaʂiakaənini
S.FORM: makasuacu nguaini, teekanicu puaiisua sua tiasiakaenini.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu ŋuaini teekaniʦu puaiisua sua tiaʂiakaenini
S.TRANSL: Similarly, (they) discussed the utensils for dining.

S.FORM: masi-ʔulu=kani sua kanakanavu, paka-sua-n=kani=kiai pakisia.
S.PHON: maʂiʔuɾukani sua kanakanavu pakasuankanikiai pakiʂia
S.FORM: masi'urukani sua kanakanavu, pakasuankanikiai pakisia.
S.PHON: maʂiʔu[r|ɾ]ukani sua kanakanavu pakasuankanikiai pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: The Kanakanavu people spoke first, and they said that to the Chinese people,

S.FORM: "nuu tee=kamu-in mu-a-ʔuna puna-punarə ia, k<um>aən=cu=kamu uuru ia, nain tia=si-a-rupan=mu k<um>aən?" misai=kan sua kanakanavu.
S.PHON: nuu teekamuin muaʔuna punapunarə ia kumaənʦukamu uuru ia nain tiaʂiarupanmu kumaən misaikan sua kanakanavu
S.FORM: "nuu teekamuin mua'una punapunare ia, k<um>aencukamu uuru ia, nain tiasiarupanmu k<um>aen?" misaikan sua kanakanavu.
S.PHON: nuu teekamuin muaʔuna punapuna[r|ɾ]e ia kumaenʦukamu uu[r|ɾ]u ia nain tiaʂia[r|ɾ]upanmu kumaen misaikan sua kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: "When you live in the wide fields, what will you use to eat rice?" the Kanakanavu people asked.

S.FORM: m-ali-vali=kani sua pakisia, "nuu tee=kim k<um>a-kaən uuru ia, tee=kimi ʔu-rupaca takupin." misai=kani sua pakisia.
S.PHON: maɾivaɾikani sua pakiʂia nuu teekim kumakaən uuru ia teekimi ʔurupaʦa takupin misaikani sua pakiʂia
S.FORM: marivarikani sua pakisia, "nuu teekim k<um>akaen uuru ia, teekimi 'urupaca takupin." misaikani sua pakisia.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]ikani sua pakiʂia nuu teekim kumakaen uu[r|ɾ]u ia teekimi ʔu[r|ɾ]upaʦa takupin misaikani sua pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: The Chinese people answered, "When we eat rice, we use bowls," the Chinese people said.

S.FORM: ma-si-naasə maamia pakisia, si nai cəʔəra-i pakisia makaasi-in.
S.PHON: maʂinaasə maamia pakiʂia ʂi nai ʦəʔərai pakiʂia makaaʂiin
S.FORM: masinaase maamia pakisia, si nai ce'erai pakisia makaasiin.
S.PHON: maʂinaase maamia pakiʂia ʂi nai ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]ai pakiʂia makaaʂiin
S.TRANSL: So, look, perhaps this is why the Chinese people became like this now.

S.FORM: ʔuuna=ʔai ʔu-rupaca taʔinsu. ʔakia ʔaratiŋ
S.PHON: ʔuunaʔai ʔurupaʦa taʔinsu ʔakia ʔaratiŋ
S.FORM: 'uuna'ai 'urupaca ta'insu. 'akia 'arating
S.PHON: ʔuunaʔai ʔu[r|ɾ]upaʦa taʔinsu ʔakia ʔa[r|ɾ]atiŋ
S.TRANSL: No one uses spoons to eat; everyone uses only chopsticks. (Kanakanavu people) use spoons; they don't have chopsticks.

S.FORM: ʔaratiŋ maamia takupin ka-vaŋvaŋ.
S.PHON: ʔaratiŋ maamia takupin kavaŋvaŋ
S.FORM: 'arating maamia takupin kavangvang.
S.PHON: ʔa[r|ɾ]atiŋ maamia takupin kavaŋvaŋ
S.TRANSL: Only chopsticks and bowls (are used).

S.FORM: pasi-vali=kan pakisia, kisa-ən=kiai kanakanavu.
S.PHON: paʂivaɾikan pakiʂia kisaənkiai kanakanavu
S.FORM: pasivarikan pakisia, kisaenkiai kanakanavu.
S.PHON: paʂiva[r|ɾ]ikan pakiʂia kisaenkiai kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: The Chinese people answered the Kanakanavu's question.

S.FORM: "tee=kamu ʔu-rupaca naumani k<um>aən?" misai=kani pakisia.
S.PHON: teekamu ʔurupaʦa naumani kumaən misaikani pakiʂia
S.FORM: "teekamu 'urupaca naumani k<um>aen?" misaikani pakisia.
S.PHON: teekamu ʔu[r|ɾ]upaʦa naumani kumaen misaikani pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: Then the Chinese asked, "What will you use to eat with?"

S.FORM: m-ali-vali=kani sua kanakanavu, "tee=kimi ʔu-rupaca taʔinsu," misai=kani kanakanavu.
S.PHON: maɾivaɾikani sua kanakanavu teekimi ʔurupaʦa taʔinsu misaikani kanakanavu
S.FORM: marivarikani sua kanakanavu, "teekimi 'urupaca ta'insu," misaikani kanakanavu.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]ikani sua kanakanavu teekimi ʔu[r|ɾ]upaʦa taʔinsu misaikani kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: The Kanakanavu replied, "When we eat, we use spoons," said the Kanakanavu.

S.FORM: vanai=kita maka-sia naturu.
S.PHON: vanaikita makaʂia naturu
S.FORM: vanaikita makasia naturu.
S.PHON: vanaikita makaʂia natu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: That's why we became fools.

S.FORM: nai, cəʔəra-i, naturu ma-maaraŋ=ta miana.
S.PHON: nai ʦəʔərai naturu mamaaraŋta miana
S.FORM: nai, ce'erai, naturu mamaarangta miana.
S.PHON: nai ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]ai natu[r|ɾ]u mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋta miana
S.TRANSL: Look, our elders in the past were stupid.

S.FORM: tee=kita k<um>a-kaən ʔu-rupaca=kita taʔinsu, ʔaisi=kita rəmər-a tantanau.
S.PHON: teekita kumakaən ʔurupaʦakita taʔinsu ʔaiʂikita rəməra tantanau
S.FORM: teekita k<um>akaen 'urupacakita ta'insu, 'aisikita remera tantanau.
S.PHON: teekita kumakaen ʔu[r|ɾ]upaʦakita taʔinsu ʔaiʂikita [r|ɾ]eme[r|ɾ]a tantanau
S.TRANSL: Hey, see what we do now. We use spoons to eat and we live in mountains.

S.FORM: vanai-n si ni-ma-kari-kari mata pakisia vanai=kita maka-sua.
S.PHON: vanain ʂi nimakarikari mata pakiʂia vanaikita makasua
S.FORM: vanain si nimakarikari mata pakisia vanaikita makasua.
S.PHON: vanain ʂi nimaka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i mata pakiʂia vanaikita makasua
S.TRANSL: This is because it was decided through our discussion with the Chinese people.

S.FORM: sua iisua ia, kaʔan pu-rəsəvə.
S.PHON: sua iisua ia kaʔan purəsəvə
S.FORM: sua iisua ia, ka'an pureseve.
S.PHON: sua iisua ia kaʔan pu[r|ɾ]eseve
S.TRANSL: That is not a lie.

S.FORM: cu-cculu pu-a-iisua, cu-cculu kari.
S.PHON: ʦuʦʦuɾu puaiisua ʦuʦʦuɾu kari
S.FORM: cuccuru puaiisua, cuccuru kari.
S.PHON: ʦuʦʦu[r|ɾ]u puaiisua ʦuʦʦu[r|ɾ]u ka[r|ɾ]i
S.TRANSL: It is a real discussion and a true story.

S.FORM: iisua maka-sua maamia kari=maku t<um>uu-tuuru kamua.
S.PHON: iisua makasua maamia karimaku tumuutuuru kamua
S.FORM: iisua makasua maamia karimaku t<um>uutuuru kamua.
S.PHON: iisua makasua maamia ka[r|ɾ]imaku tumuutuu[r|ɾ]u kamua
S.TRANSL: This is what I have been telling you.

S.FORM: ŋuaci kari=maku, ʔakia cucuma-in.
S.PHON: ŋuatʂi karimaku ʔakia ʦuʦumain
S.FORM: nguaci karimaku, 'akia cucumain.
S.PHON: ŋuatʂi ka[r|ɾ]imaku ʔakia ʦuʦumain
S.TRANSL: My words end here; nothing more.
